# Nomadar Adds Uruguay to Its International Youth Soccer Network


10 Nov, 2026


|[Press Releases](https://investor.nomadar.com/category/press-releases/)


New Cádiz CF–Nomadar International Camp will bring Spanish professional soccer training to approximately 100 young players, strengthening connections between Latin America, the United States, and Europe.


**MARSHALL, Texas, November 10, 2026** – Nomadar Corp. (Nasdaq: NOMA) (“Nomadar” or the “Company”), a global sports, tourism, technology, and experiential infrastructure company, today announced the launch of its first youth soccer camp in Uruguay the Cádiz CF–Nomadar International Campus, scheduled for January 11–15, 2027, in Punta del Este. The initiative further strengthens Nomadar’s growing presence in Latin America and its strategy of connecting sports development opportunities across the United States, Latin America, and Europe.


Organized in collaboration with Cádiz CF and local partner Kilómetro Deportivo, the five-day program is expected to welcome approximately 100 young players ages 8 and older. Participants are expected to train under Cádiz CF coaches using the methodology of the High Performance Training (HPT) program developed by Nomadar and Cádiz CF, gaining firsthand exposure to the coaching techniques, training philosophy, and standards of Spanish professional soccer.


The program will also feature a talent identification component, with two standout participants to be selected to travel to Cádiz, Spain, for a weeklong training experience with the club in April 2027.


## Expanding an Established International Development Platform


The Uruguay initiative builds on Nomadar’s experience delivering international youth soccer development programs through its collaboration with Cádiz CF, a historic Spanish professional soccer club competing within the LaLiga system.


At the center of this international offering is the HPT program, which combines professional coaching expertise, structured player development, and immersive training experiences in Spain. Through its established training methodology, Nomadar and Cádiz CF provide young athletes from international markets with access to the methodology and environment of Spanish professional soccer.


Over the past three years, more than 350 young players from the United States, Japan, Mexico, Germany, Ecuador, Nigeria, and Azerbaijan have participated in the program, demonstrating its international reach and the growing demand for high-quality soccer development experiences.


The program’s track record also includes players who have earned international recognition, including Mario Lobato, called up to Spain’s U15 national team, and Jan Saltzman, called up to Sweden’s U17 national team.


By extending this model to Uruguay, Nomadar continues to develop its international sports platform, creating new pathways for young athletes while strengthening the connections between its activities in the Americas and its training programs in Europe.


## Bringing the Cádiz CF Experience to Uruguay


Pablo Sánchez, Head of International at Cádiz CF and Director of International Sports Projects at Nomadar, commented:


“Uruguay is an exciting addition to our international development activities and a country with a remarkable soccer tradition. Our goal is to bring young players the same coaching philosophy and professional standards we apply in Cádiz, while giving them the opportunity to develop their skills, experience a different training environment, and connect with Spanish soccer. For two participants, that journey will continue with a training experience at Cádiz CF in April.”


Nomadar and Cádiz CF will work with Kilómetro Deportivo, a Uruguayan sports organization focused on youth development and international sporting experiences, to coordinate the program locally. Its representative, Guillermo Cabana, also founded La Costa Fútbol in 2017 alongside Andrés Cabrera. The organization operates two sports complexes in the Canelones region, offering soccer schools, leagues, and international development activities.


“For us, bringing the Cádiz CF and Nomadar experience to Uruguay represents an important opportunity for young players and their families,” said Guillermo Cabana of Kilómetro Deportivo. “We believe soccer can open doors to new experiences, learning, and personal growth. This program will allow participants to train with professional coaches, experience a different soccer culture, and build connections that extend beyond the field. We see this as the beginning of a long-term relationship.”


Technical preparations are expected to begin on December 21, 2026, with an online coordination session between Cádiz CF’s coaching staff and the Uruguayan organizers to finalize training groups and program logistics.


The Punta del Este campus represents another step in Nomadar’s international growth strategy, leveraging its sports expertise, established training methodology, and network of partners to bring professional soccer development experiences to new markets and connect young athletes with opportunities across continents.


**About Nomadar**


Nomadar Corp. is a U.S.-based company operating at the intersection of sports, tourism, technology, and health. A subsidiary of Cádiz CF, a 115-year-old professional soccer club competing within the La Liga system, Nomadar develops innovative projects that connect global audiences through experiences that combine health, entertainment, and digital engagement.


The Company is also advancing the JP Financial Arena real estate development project for a multi-purpose event center in southern Europe, designed to host international sports, cultural, and corporate events. Nomadar’s mission is to create sustainable, technology-driven platforms that enhance the connection between sports, community, and health.
